prompt: A small retail chain decided to sell stock to raise capital. Under what form of business organization does the retail chain operate?
explanation: Corporation. A corporation is the only form of business organization that is permitted to sell stock. The other alternatives are types of businesses that must use personal funds, borrow, or take on new partners to raise capital.

prompt: One of the ways demand for a product affects its distribution is through the
explanation: Decisions about storage. If demand for a product is fluctuating, the company may decide to rent temporary storage space for the product until it has a better idea of what regular demand will be. If a product has a seasonal demand but production goes on all year long, the company will probably own its own warehouse because of the length of time the product must be stored between seasons. The product itself determines the special handling that is required. The company size affects the use of computerized inventory control. Demand does not generally affect the regulation of distribution activities.

prompt: Which of the following is the most common channel of distribution for consumer goods:
choices: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
Producer to agents to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
explanation: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer. This is the most common distribution method for consumer goods. The manufacturer sells to the wholesaler who then handles the sales, warehousing, and distribution of the goods to retailers. Producer to consumer is more likely to be used for direct contact by manufacturer to consumer, such as Avon. Producer to retailer to consumer is the channel used for merchandise that dates quickly or needs servicing, such as fashion items or automobiles. Producer to agents to wholesaler to retailer to consumer is used by producers who do not want to handle their own sales to retailers.

prompt: A manufacturer selling its products through a toll-free phone system, a company web site, and several retailers is a legal example of
explanation: Dual distribution. When a manufacturer uses more than one channel to reach consumers, it is known as dual distribution. Dual distribution is legal as long as it promotes competition. When a supplier requires an intermediary to purchase other products in its line, as well as the initial purchase, it is known as a tying agreement. Exclusive dealing occurs when a manufacturer forbids an intermediary from carrying a competitor's product. Restricted sales territories prohibit intermediaries from selling products outside a designated area.

prompt: Which of the following is a marketing activity that a retail chain should coordinate with distribution in order to successfully sell its product:
explanation: Promotion. Promotion is a marketing function that communicates information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. In order to successfully sell its product, a retail chain needs to coordinate all the components of marketing, which include distribution, promotion, product, and price. For example, if a retail chain develops an effective distribution system but fails to promote the product, customers will not know about the product or want it, although it is readily available. Orientation is job preparation or induction training for new employees. Production is the creation of goods and services from economic resources. Competition is the rivalry between two or more businesses to attract customer dollars.

prompt: In which of the following situations might vertical conflict occur in a channel of distribution:
choices: Two similar retailers compete for the same target market.
A manufacturer decides to sell its products on its web site.
Distributors for a product agree to charge the same price.
An organization sells additional franchises in the same city.
explanation: A manufacturer decides to sell its products on its web site. Vertical conflict in a channel of distribution occurs when there is disagreement between different levels of members in the same channel. An example of a vertical channel is a manufacturer selling to wholesalers who then sell to retailers. Conflict may occur if the manufacturer decides to sell its products on its web site as well as sell them to wholesalers. Both the wholesalers and the retailers may feel that they will lose sales because the products are available directly to the ultimate consumer. Horizontal conflict may occur if an organization sells additional franchises in the same city or if two similar retailers compete for the same target market. Distributors for a product agreeing to charge the same price is price fixing.

prompt: In order to use oral communication effectively, you need to
explanation: Pronounce your words correctly. The correct use and pronunciation of words is essential to effective oral communication. Mispronunciation creates an unfavorable impression, it can create embarrassment for the speaker, and it may also fail to communicate the intended message. Trying to impress listeners may create a barrier to good communication. It is not necessary to know your listeners in order to communicate effectively. You need to attract and hold your listeners' attention, not distract them.

prompt: Why is it important for a retail store's employees to ask relevant questions?
explanation: To clarify meanings. Relevant questions are those questions that pertain to the issue at hand. They are asked to obtain information. A retail store's employees should ask relevant questions in order to clarify the meaning of statements or instructions. By asking relevant questions, the retail store's employees can obtain additional explanations to help them understand what they are expected to do. A retail store's employees do not ask questions to send messages, offer suggestions, or make statements.

prompt: One reason retail employees often use note cards when making oral presentations is because the cards help them to
explanation: Remember key points. Retail employees often write brief notes on small cards to help them remember to discuss important points they want to present to the audience. The notes serve as a guide to help employees stay focused on the information they need to present and keep them from getting off track. The notes are often a mini-outline of the presentation. Employees do not use note cards to look important, write down questions, or memorize the data.

prompt: When a customer asks for a product that is sold in another department of the store, the salesperson should
choices: tell the customer s/he is in the wrong department.
give the customer directions to the other department.
tell the customer to go to the other department.
show the customer what is available in his/her department.
explanation: Give the customer directions to the other department. When a customer asks for a product that the employee knows is available in another location, an example of a courteous response would be, "We don't have that in this department, but it is sold in Department C which is opposite the elevators on the second floor." The employee has provided customer assistance and created goodwill toward the store. Telling the customer to go to the other department is inappropriate. The customer has asked for a specific item and is not likely to be interested in other items at the moment. Telling the customer s/he is in the wrong department is a rude response that is also not helpful.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a customer inquiry about a lawn mower that a hardware store employee might need product knowledge of in order to handle:
explanation: "Is it designed to last?" Customers often inquire as to the design or construction of a product, such as a lawn mower. Hardware store employees should be well-informed about the design and construction of products in order to explain their features and benefits and encourage customers to buy. Knowledgeable employees can effectively handle customers' inquiries about products. "Is there a return policy?", "Is financing available?", and "Is delivery included?" are inquiries about a store's policies rather than about the product.

prompt: The most important business policy affecting customers directly is the ___________ policy.
explanation: Product. The most important business policy affecting customers is the product policy. Management decides what kind of products to offer, and these products attract customers more than any other feature of the business. Service policies provide special features that other, similar businesses may not offer, such as delivery or installation. Credit policies are the arrangements by which customers can purchase now and pay later. Promotional policies are guidelines affecting the kinds of special activities, such as contests and prizes, that businesses use to attract customers and to increase sales.

prompt: What is one way that an efficient receiving process often benefits a hardware store?
explanation: Increases sales and profits. An efficient receiving process may increase sales and profits by having goods available when customers want them. Properly receiving goods does not decrease sales and profits. The accuracy of the receiving process does not necessarily decrease or increase labor expenses, but may help to control them.

prompt: Merchandise shipments received by your store include items about to be advertised, seasonal items, valuable goods, and basic stock reorders. Which items would be processed last?
explanation: Basic stock reorders. When many shipments of merchandise are received at the same time, priorities should be assigned to the items to determine the order in which they should be processed. By having the most-needed merchandise available first, the business can increase its sales. Top priority for processing merchandise should be given to merchandise that is about to be advertised, valuable goods, and seasonal items. Basic stock reorders should be assigned the lowest processing priority because there should be a sufficient quantity of this merchandise available for sale since it is reordered on a regular basis.

prompt: Receiving clerks usually count each item in a shipment and mark it off the purchase order in order to
explanation: Identify discrepancies. One way to identify shipping discrepancies is for receiving clerks to count the items in a shipment and mark them off the purchase order. By counting each item, the receiving clerks will find out if certain items are missing or if more items were shipped than ordered. Labeling merchandise, distributing stock, and warehousing excess goods are other aspects of receiving.

prompt: What do many businesses need to do regularly in order to maintain adequate inventory levels?
explanation: Reorder. Many businesses regularly reorder goods that are used routinely in order to maintain adequate inventory levels. Some businesses, such as restaurants and grocery stores, reorder daily in order to have adequate stock on hand. Other businesses may reorder every few months depending on how quickly they use or resell items. Most businesses develop annual budgets to plan for the amount of money that will be needed to regularly reorder goods. Promoting and scheduling are not activities that are involved in maintaining adequate inventory levels.

prompt: Osgood's Discount Store has hired a firm to count the stock that the store has on hand. This business is conducting a ___________ inventory.
explanation: Physical. Physical inventories are taken by most retailers at periodic intervals. Some retailers hire an outside company to count inventory. A perpetual, or book, inventory updates inventory records on a continuous basis with information about sales, returns, and any other changes affecting stock counts. A visual inventory system tags goods with color codes so that buyers know from glancing at the stock how long it has been on hand.

prompt: Which of the following is information that a retail store can obtain by using a unit inventory control system:
explanation: Stock returned by customers. Unit inventory control keeps track of inventory according to the number of physical units of stock. It tells the store how much inventory it owns. The unit inventory control system provides the store with information as to the stock returned by customers. This information lets the store know that it has items in stock that customers do not want and might need to be reduced in price in order to sell. The dollar inventory control system provides a store with information as to projected losses from sales, capital available to buy goods, and sales totals from previous years.

prompt: Retailers with point-of-sale systems can easily monitor their stock levels on a regular basis by
explanation: Reviewing computer printouts. In a point-of-sale system, all transactions are recorded as they occur, and stock records are being perpetually updated by the computer. This method provides information much more easily and quickly than tabulating sales receipts by hand. An annual count of stock is done once a year and gives accurate figures only at that particular time. A FIFO system is a method of managing stock in which the oldest stock (first in) is sold first (first out).

prompt: The new toy on the market was in high demand but available only in limited quantities. The local toy store decided to take advantage of the situation by
explanation: Increasing the price. Retailers may temporarily mark up the price of fad or specialty items to take advantage of high demand and limited availability. Consumers sometimes are willing to pay more for certain goods, but retailers are careful not to create bad feelings by increasing prices excessively. The store would not be able to order more toys because of their limited availability. The retailer would not put on sale or store items that were in high demand but available only in limited quantities.

prompt: Because individuals and businesses are the primary decision makers, while government helps to regulate and control the system, the United States private enterprise system is considered a __________ economic system.
explanation: Mixed. The United States is considered a mixed system with elements of business and government control. A traditional economic system is one in which people produce only what they must have in order to exist; all economic decisions are based on habit and tradition. In a command economy, all or many of the means of production and distribution are owned and controlled by government. A socialist system is a modified command system in which government owns the basic means of production and allows private ownership of business as well.

prompt: A store entered into an agreement with its supplier stating that the supplier would not sell to anyone else in his town, thereby eliminating the store's competition. What federal act is this store and its supplier violating?
explanation: Clayton Act. The Clayton Act is a federal regulation intended to prevent specific business actions that might prohibit competition, such as tying agreements and exclusive agreements. The Celler-Kefauver Act protects competitors from takeovers that would limit competition. The Robinson-Patman Act prohibits price discrimination. The Sherman Antitrust Act is intended to prevent monopolies.

prompt: An economy with a high unemployment level tends to have
explanation: A lower rate of inflation. When a lot of people are out of work, they lose their buying power, which means less money is in circulation. Because unemployed people have less disposable income, the demand for goods and services is low, which tends to slow or lower the rate of inflation (rise in prices). The amount of monetary policies that the Fed establishes does not affect unemployment rates. When the GDP grows, an economic expansion is occurring, which indicates that people and businesses are spending money, and the unemployment levels are low.

prompt: The cultural and social environments of other countries are important considerations when retailers make decisions about
explanation: Global trade. Global trade is the buying and selling of goods and services between nations throughout the world. When retailers make decisions about global trade, they consider the cultural and social characteristics of other countries. This is important because the differences in culture have an impact on the types of goods and services that people in other countries want and need. For example, culture often dictates the type of clothing that people wear and the type of food that they eat. Retailers need to know this to avoid trying to sell inappropriate products in other countries. The cultural and social environments of other countries are not important considerations when retailers make decisions about shipping methods, online access, or payment systems.

prompt: Why are many large retailers expanding by opening outlets in foreign countries?
explanation: Domestic market is saturated. Many retailers have saturated the market in their home countries; therefore, the only way for them to expand is to enter foreign markets. The growth of international trade makes this possible because many trade barriers no longer exist due to agreements between countries to promote international trade. Consequently, many retailers are taking advantage of this opportunity to expand into countries that are entering the global economy and whose citizens are beginning to have disposable income. Lower production costs are reasons that some retailers buy goods from foreign countries. Transportation in many foreign countries is not efficient because of lack of development. The employee base may be large, but that is not a reason for opening outlets in foreign countries. Retailers open outlets to expand and sell more goods.

prompt: When your level of self-esteem is low, this causes you to have
explanation: Doubts about yourself. When self-doubts are present, self-esteem has dropped. These doubts and your low level of self-esteem may keep you from having confidence in your own ability or an appreciation for life. A low level of self-esteem does not necessarily cause difficulty with visualization-the practice of imagining yourself in possession of a present or desired strength. Visualization is a method of overcoming low levels of self-esteem.

prompt: Altering personal behavior in order to show enthusiasm requires discipline and
explanation: Practice. Changing personal behavior requires an individual to have enough self-discipline to practice the new, improved behavior until it becomes routine. Leadership is taking positive steps to influence and to guide others. Empathy is the ability to put yourself in another person's place. There is no monetary cost, or expense, involved in altering behavior.

prompt: A person who is willing to act without having to be told to do so is said to possess the trait of
explanation: Initiative. A person with initiative is willing to accept/seek additional duties and responsibilities without having to be urged. The term empathy refers to a person's sensitivity to and understanding of others. Tact refers to a person's ability to express his/her ideas and beliefs without offending others. Selfishness means being overly concerned about one's own needs and interests.

prompt: If a large outlet mall allows its employees to dispose of contaminated water by pouring it into a nearby stream, the mall might face possible
explanation: Government intervention. Sometimes, businesses such as outlet malls allow their employees to take actions that result in public pressure for government intervention. Polluting the environment is an action that might force the government to intervene and impose regulations to control what a business is permitted to do. Government intervention may result in guidelines that make it more difficult and costly to do business. Trade restrictions limit the quantity of goods that can move into or out of a country. Industry probably would condemn, rather than recognize, a business that contributed to environmental pollution. If a business allows its employees to pollute, it has the support of management.

prompt: The purpose of constructive criticism is to
choices: None of these answers is correct.
explanation: Motivate people to improve. Constructive criticism is intended to help individuals by suggesting ways they can improve. It is given in a positive manner, not as a negative judgment, and it does not question personal values.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of working effectively with a coworker:
explanation: Sharing tools and job information. Working effectively with a coworker can be demonstrated in many ways, one of which is sharing tools and job information. This is an example of interdependence among workers. Being on time and accepting constructive criticism indicate a willingness to cooperate with management. Participating in the grapevine, an informal communication channel in most companies, is a common occurrence but not an example of working effectively with a coworker.

prompt: Lisa charges a small gift shop to use the extra space in the building she owns. Which of the following is Lisa's source of income:
explanation: Rent. Income is a money resource owners receive for supplying goods and services. As a resource owner, Lisa is supplying retail space and receiving rent payments from the gift shop, so she is receiving income. A salary is a form of income that is money payments for labor. A dividend is the sum of money paid to an investor or stockholder as earnings on an investment. Interest is the money payment for the use of borrowed money.

prompt: An advantage to retailers of offering credit is that credit customers
choices: spend more time deciding to buy.
have little effect on store profits.
often buy impulse items more freely.
explanation: Often buy impulse items more freely. Credit encourages customers to buy more freely. Credit customers like being able to buy without worrying about whether they have the cash on hand to pay for their purchases. As a result, they may buy impulse items that catch their attention. Store profit is affected by credit customers, who often spend less time making buying decisions than other customers. Credit accounts are not always paid on time, and, for the retailer, collecting past-due accounts is a disadvantage of the credit system.

prompt: One of the reasons why a furniture store should examine its profit-and-loss statement is to
explanation: Understand its entire financial situation. A profit-and-loss statement is a furniture store's financial picture that lists all revenues and expenses for a certain time period. Stores examine their profit-and-loss statements in order to understand their entire financial situation, because the statements are a summary of transactions that show net profit before and after taxes by analyzing sales, purchases, cost of goods sold, and operating expenses for a specific time period. Balance of trade is the difference between the value of a nation's exports and its imports. Stores gather information from all departments and divisions and organize the statistics in categories to develop the profit-and-loss statement.

prompt: Cornucopia Specialty Gifts charges an 18% handling fee for custom orders. The fee is based on the total amount of the order. The invoice indicates that the total order amount is $249.00. What is the handling charge for the order?
explanation: $44.82. When preparing invoices, retailers consider all costs including any handling fee. To calculate the handling fee, multiply the amount of the order by the percentage ($249.00 x 18% or .18 = $44.82).

prompt: What is the best source of information that the owner of a new gift shop could use to find out how to collect sales tax?
explanation: The state taxation agency. Each state has its own name for this agency, which establishes procedures for collecting and remitting the tax, as well as explaining the types of services that are taxable. The Internal Revenue Service is concerned with federal taxes. The chamber of commerce and financial institutions may be able to refer you to the appropriate state agency, but they would not have the tax information.

prompt: The purpose of maintaining daily financial transactions is to keep track of the retailer's
explanation: Income and expenses. Financial transactions, such as selling products and paying bills, affect the financial condition of the retailer. The purpose of maintaining daily financial transactions is to make sure the retailer has sufficient income to cover expenses, and is financially sound. For example, transactions that bring in money are necessary to offset the bills that the retailer must pay. Retailers do not maintain daily financial transactions to keep track of payroll and benefits, assets and liabilities, or stocks and bonds.

prompt: Being able to understand and predict future risks is one of the benefits to a retailer of gathering
explanation: Marketing information. Marketing information is all of the marketing-related data available from inside and outside the retailer. It includes information about past situations and what is happening now. By gathering marketing information, retailers often are able to understand and predict the risks that might occur in the future and take steps to control those risks. For example, if current marketing information indicates that one product is losing popularity, a retailer can modify the product or repackage it to be more appealing. As a result, the retailer might avoid losing customers, which is a future risk. Gathering advertising data, selling resources, and pricing results will not help retailers to understand and predict future risks.

prompt: When a retail chain uses data from its marketing-information management system to determine the retail chain's current business position and the direction in which the retail chain is headed, the retail chain is preparing a
explanation: Situation analysis. The marketing-information management system can provide the internal and external data used in a situation analysis: a determination of a retail chain's current business situation and the direction in which the retail chain is headed. A sales forecast is a prediction of future sales over a specific period of time. Marketing-research reports result from the systematic gathering, recording, and analyzing of data about a specific problem. Data analysis is the function of a marketing-information management system that involves evaluating information and putting it in a format that is useful to a business.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a home improvement store obtaining marketing information about consumers in a way that might be considered unethical:
choices: Offering a free product in exchange for personal data
Sending questionnaires to a specific audience
explanation: Offering a free product in exchange for personal data. Certain ways of obtaining marketing information may be considered unethical even though they are legal. An example is offering free products in exchange for personal data. Consumers may be persuaded to provide information that they normally would not provide simply because the offer is so tempting or they need the product being offered. Furthermore, consumers have no guarantee that the home improvement store will keep the personal data confidential. In some cases, stores try to obtain this information in order to sell it to others. Most stores follow ethical procedures when obtaining marketing information about consumers. These procedures might include conducting a random survey, sending questionnaires to a specific audience, and developing a scientific experiment.

prompt: Why do many bookstores place a cookie on a user's hard drive when the user visits the bookstore's web site?
choices: To track the number of times the user makes a purchase
To make it easy for the user to find the web site
To regulate the user's access to information
To guarantee that the web site is secure
explanation: To track the number of times the user makes a purchase. Many bookstores that have web sites place a cookie, which is a type of information, on a user's hard drive when the user visits that site. Then, the next time a user visits that site, the site's computer recognizes the user because of the cookie. A bookstore's marketing-information managers use cookies to maintain user information and track how many times a user visits a specific web site or makes a purchase online. This type of data allows marketing-information managers to customize web sites in order to appeal to the preferences and habits of the customers who are visiting their sites. Cookies make it possible for bookstores to obtain marketing information. They do not make it easy for the user to find the web site, regulate the user's access to information, or guarantee that the web site is secure.

prompt: Retailers often make decisions regarding changes in their product lines by analyzing data from their
explanation: Sales invoices. An invoice is the formal, printed record of a sale that includes all necessary information as to the buyer, the seller, items purchased, amounts, prices, delivery date, credit, discount terms, and other data regarding the sales transaction. Invoices usually possess key marketing and sales data in one location. Researchers often use this data to analyze information, such as product movement and account activity. Accounting reports summarize financial data as it relates to business activities. Freight bills are invoices that relate to the transportation of goods. Although freight bills might be used in marketing research, freight information is often included on the sales invoice. Utilization summary is not a marketing term that is commonly used.

prompt: Hardware stores collect marketing information from other sources in order to find out what is happening in the
explanation: External environment. It is important for hardware stores to collect marketing information from other sources in order to find out what is happening in the external environment. They need to know about the economy in general, any changes in demographics, legal or political situations, etc. This type of information is not available from within the hardware store but must be collected from outside sources, such as industry or trade organizations, government agencies, and consumer reports. Hardware stores use both external and internal information in order to make marketing decisions and solve problems. Hardware stores collect internal information from their own research departments. Internal information is also available from the parent corporation and the organization itself.

prompt: What marketing function helps retailers decide to whom to sell?
explanation: Marketing-information management. Marketing-information management is a marketing function that involves gathering, accessing, synthesizing, evaluating, and disseminating information for use in making business decisions. This information helps retailers define their markets. Product/Service management involves obtaining, developing, maintaining, and improving a product or service mix in response to market opportunities. The pricing function involves determining and adjusting prices to maximize return and meet customers' perceptions of value. Financing is a business function rather than a marketing function .

prompt: Reselling merchandise to customers in the target market is an example of
explanation: Retailing. Retailing involves buying goods and selling them to the ultimate consumer. Retailers buy merchandise from vendors and resell that merchandise to customers. Marketing is an organizational function and a set of processes for creating, communicating, and delivering value to customers and for managing customer relationships in ways that benefit the organization and its stakeholders. Trading involves exchanging one item for another rather than selling the item. Retailers purchase merchandise to resell.

prompt: Would a successful retail chain ever change its marketing strategy?
choices: Yes, changes in the marketplace require changes in marketing strategy.
Yes, a retail chain should have no more than two marketing strategies.
No, changing marketing strategies is a complicated process.
No, once a retail chain has a workable strategy, it should always be used.
explanation: Yes, changes in the marketplace require changes in marketing strategy. Changes such as price increases, new competition, or an increase in operating expenses require that retail chains have flexible strategies. A responsible retail chain will be prepared to redesign its strategies as needed.

prompt: What type of information do retailers include in their marketing plans?
explanation: Pricing strategies. A marketing plan is a set of procedures or strategies for attracting the target customer to a retailer. An important part of a marketing plan is the pricing strategies that a retailer will use to attract those customers. Retailers want their prices to be low enough to appeal to customers but high enough to cover costs and earn a profit. Retailers analyze a variety of information about expenses, prices charged by competitors, and customers' wants in order to decide how to price their products. Retailers do not include information about billing methods, payroll systems, or accounting procedures in their marketing plans.

prompt: Why should a bookstore evaluate its internal environment when changes are occurring in its external environment?
explanation: To remain competitive. When a bookstore's external environment changes, it should evaluate its internal environment in order to remain competitive. External changes, such as industry growth or a slowdown in the economy, often make it necessary for a company to change the way it does business. These types of external changes might make it more difficult for a bookstore to compete and remain successful. In response to external changes, a bookstore might update its advertising, revise its pricing, and improve its distribution in order to remain competitive.

prompt: A wholesale distributor of ready-to-wear clothing would like to track its customers geographically. Which software application would be most effective?
explanation: Database. A database is a collection (or file) of related information about a specific topic. Many businesses collect information about their customers and store this information in computer databases. Then, businesses can access this information at any time for a variety of reasons such as tracking customers geographically. Spreadsheet software is used to organize, calculate, and analyze numerical data. Word-processing software is used to create text documents. The Internet is not a software application program.

prompt: Retailers often use word-processing computer software to produce
explanation: Detailed reports, memos, and contracts. Retailers use word-processing software to create a variety of business-related documents, including reports, memos, contracts, business plans, letters, and tables. Spreadsheets are generated by other types of software programs (e.g., Excel) that organize, calculate, and analyze numerical information. Although many word-processing applications have basic drawing capabilities to produce simple graphics, the more complex graphic elements are generally created by special graphics and design programs (e.g., Freehand).

prompt: Hardware stores often monitor internal inventory records to obtain the information needed to
explanation: Plan special sales. Hardware stores monitor internal inventory records to keep track of the type and quantity of products that are in stock. By monitoring this information, stores can identify an oversupply of certain products or products that are slow sellers. The inventory records help stores decide when it would be appropriate to plan a special sale to get rid of excess inventory or slow-selling items. Keeping these items in stock ties up money that the store could use to buy new products that customers want to buy. Stores do not monitor internal inventory records to obtain the information needed to organize new displays, evaluate vendors, or create safety rules.

prompt: Electronic sensors, closed-circuit television, locked display cases, and security guards are security devices used to help businesses prevent
explanation: Shoplifting. Shoplifting is the theft of goods by customers. Customers may steal goods from counters, displays, dressing rooms, or any place they find items. Security devices help prevent or reveal these thefts. Pilferage is the theft of small sums of money or inexpensive items from the business by an employee. Burglary is illegal entry into a building to commit a theft. Fraud is deceiving or cheating a business out of money or property.

prompt: Large, nationwide retail chains often use which of the following types of buying systems:
explanation: Decentralized. Decentralized is a way of organizing purchasing in which responsibility and authority are distributed among many departments and individuals. Many nationwide retail chains have decentralized their purchasing operations because they have grown so large that central buying can no longer effectively purchase for geographically distant stores. Standardized is something that is always done in the same way. Centralized purchasing is a way of organizing purchasing in which responsibility and authority are held in one department and/or by a few individuals. Specialized is concentrating on a limited line of endeavor.

prompt: What is often the best way for a retailer to increase its profit?
explanation: Reduce expenses. Decreasing expenses is perhaps the best way that retailers can help to increase profit. Retailers have control over many of their expenses and can take measures to reduce them. For example, they can eliminate some free services and encourage workers to turn off lights and equipment when not being used, in order to save money on energy costs. Raising prices will not increase profits unless customers are willing to pay the higher prices. Tax rates are regulated by government. If retailers improve sales, they might increase their profits if the rate of sales is proportionately higher than the expense involved.

prompt: Coins should be placed in cash drawers in order of increasing monetary value from
explanation: Right to left. As you move across the cash drawer from right to left, the monetary value of coins should increase. Therefore, you should arrange pennies in the far right-hand front compartment, then nickels, then dimes, and then quarters.

prompt: Time management helps to reduce stress because it
choices: encourages procrastination in planning necessary activities.
provides less time for rest and relaxation.
allows adequate time for personal and professional activities.
increases feelings of pressure and tension.
explanation: Allows adequate time for personal and professional activities. The use of time-management techniques forces us to take care of important activities immediately, which relieves pressure and tension. It allows more time for rest and relaxation. This will ultimately reduce stress.

prompt: What department of a large retail chain should a job seeker contact to find out whether the chain has job openings?
explanation: Human resources. The human resources department in a large retail chain handles such personnel responsibilities as hiring of staff, keeping personnel records, and administering benefit programs. Most human resources departments expect to answer inquiries from job seekers about possible job openings. The payroll department issues paychecks to employees. The credit department handles customer credit accounts. Training and development may be part of human resources, but it is set up to provide assistance to current employees or new hires, not job applicants.

prompt: What would be the best response to write on a job application form for the reason that you left your last job if you quit because you felt your supervisor was unfair?
choices: Unable to get along with supervisor
explanation: Left for a better job. When providing information about previous jobs, you should present a positive picture of yourself and your former employers. Avoid saying anything that puts you or a former employer in a negative light. Therefore, comments such as "unable to get along with supervisor," "unfair supervisor," and "unpleasant working environment" should be avoided. Telling a potential employer that you left to find a better job says nothing negative about your abilities or those of former employers.

prompt: When considering candidates for promotion, employers often base decisions on employees' seniority and their ability to
explanation: Learn new skills. When people are promoted, they are often required to perform additional or different tasks than those performed in their previous positions. Employers often want to promote people who are willing to learn new skills and have the ability to learn them in a timely manner. Making recommendations, leading staff meetings, and working long hours are not always expectations or responsibilities in all jobs.

prompt: John is a manager in a local retail store. What professional organization will be the most appropriate for him to join?
choices: International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions
explanation: The National Retail Federation. Since John is employed in a retail store, he would benefit by being a member of a professional retail organization. The National Retail Federation is an organization whose members operate department, chain, mass merchandiser, and specialty stores. Professionals in the banking industry will benefit by being a member of a banking organization, such as the American Bankers Association. If he were manager of an amusement park, the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions would better suit him. Managers or owners of furniture stores would benefit by being a member of a professional furnishing association, such as the National Home Furnishing Association.

prompt: What career in retailing might require an individual to have extensive knowledge about creative design principles and lighting techniques?
explanation: Visual merchandising. Visual merchandising includes activities that attract retail customers to products to stimulate interest and buying. Visual merchandisers often schedule, design, assemble, and dismantle display windows and work to create a unique selling atmosphere as determined by management's objectives. To create an effective environment, visual merchandisers must understand artistic design principles (e.g., color, balance) and how to use light for optimal results. Accounting is a business function that is responsible for keeping and interpreting financial records. Inventory control is a function related to the distribution process and is responsible for maintaining appropriate levels of stock for a retailer. Security is responsible for developing, maintaining, and executing safety procedures for a retail establishment.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason for the growth of non-store retailing:
choices: Fewer ways to buy products than in the past
explanation: Increased use of the Internet. Increased use of the Internet is a major reason for the growth of non-store retailing. More and more consumers are shopping online, and there are many buying options that weren't available in the past, such as telephone ordering and mail ordering. Increased retail competition makes non-store retailing even more important to many businesses. More and more retailers are using multi-channel retailing all the time.

prompt: Home-improvement stores might consider increasing their prices during times when
explanation: Economic conditions are good. Home-improvement stores need to be willing to adjust their prices. These adjustments can be increases or decreases, depending on the circumstances faced by the store. When economic conditions are good, the home-improvement store might increase its prices because customers are less cautious with their spending. Home-improvement stores often decrease their prices when goods and services are plentiful, when customers have less money to spend, and when many people are unemployed.

prompt: A law is established to ensure that retailers include pricing terms in their advertisements. The law is designed to discourage retailers from practicing __________ pricing strategies.
explanation: Deceptive. Deceptive advertising practices employ techniques that lead a customer to believe that the product holds greater value than it actually does. For example, a retailer publishes a very low price in a newspaper advertisement for a specific product. A customer enters the store with the intention of purchasing the product at that price. However, the customer finds out that certain criteria must be met to receive the published price. The retailer used a published price under false pretenses to get customers into the store. Inequitable, elastic, and compliant are not terms that are widely used to describe misleading advertising and pricing practices.

prompt: The opening of a large discount store is likely to force the small neighborhood stores to __________ in order to compete.
explanation: Lower their prices. Competition from large discount stores often forces smaller stores to lower their prices in an effort to compete. Small stores could not afford to hire more employees, remodel their facilities, or plan special events in order to compete with discount stores.

prompt: What is one question that a company needs to answer about a product that is in the introductory stage of its life cycle?
choices: Does the product need to be modernized?
How can we make the public aware of our product?
Should we take the product off the market?
explanation: How can we make the public aware of our product? In the introductory stage of the product life cycle, the most important focus for a company is to draw attention to its product. Without awareness, sales cannot occur and the product/company cannot gain market share. A company wouldn't consider taking a product off the market immediately after it is introduced. Regionalizing and modernizing the product are considerations for products that are in the decline stage of the product life cycle.

prompt: One way that advances in technology are impacting the product/service management function is by making it possible for appliance manufacturers to
explanation: Improve existing products. As a result of advances in technology, new materials and operating techniques have been developed. These materials and techniques have made it possible for appliance manufacturers to improve existing products. This impacts the product/service management function because it enables manufacturers to extend the life of existing appliances and keep them on the market. Manufacturers have found that it is usually less expensive to update existing products than to develop entirely new products. Advances in technology are allowing businesses to do this. Advances in technology often help to reduce human errors but cannot completely eliminate them. Advances in technology often make production systems more complex because they rely on complicated computer systems. Manufacturers are not able to control customer preferences.

prompt: Why are many retail businesses looking for ways to reuse products by turning them into new products?
choices: To solve the ethical problem of planned obsolescence
To save money on the process of product development
To encourage customers to buy reconditioned products
To position products as being technologically advanced
explanation: To solve the ethical problem of planned obsolescence. Because of continual advances in technology, some products become obsolete very quickly. Retail businesses that make these products are often aware of the ethical issues involved in producing goods that have a short life span because of their effect on the natural resources that are needed to produce them. To handle this problem, some retail businesses are looking for ways to recycle all or parts of these products and reuse them or turn them into new products. This enables retail businesses to preserve natural resources and to be ethical while producing products that become obsolete quickly. It is often expensive for businesses to develop ways of reusing products or turning them into new products. The retail businesses are reusing the products rather than reconditioning them and selling them to customers. Retail businesses do not turn products into new products to position them as being technologically advanced.

prompt: Many appliance stores advertise that they sell only products that have been manufactured according to industry standards in order to let customers know that the appliances they buy are
explanation: Safe to use. Some grades and standards can be used to indicate product safety. Many appliance stores advertise that they sell only products that have been manufactured according to industry standards in order to let customers know that the store's appliances are safe to use. Appliance stores do not advertise that their products have been manufactured according to industry standards in order to let customers know that the appliances are costly to buy. Appliances that are manufactured according to industry standards are not necessarily energy-efficient or maintenance-free.

prompt: Jim purchased an electric fryer from Chairman Department Store. The salesperson stated that the fryer comes with a one-year written warranty and, if it doesn't work properly during that year, the product can be returned (with the original receipt) to be fixed or replaced free-of-charge. What type of warranty did Jim receive with the fryer?
explanation: Express. An express warranty is a promise expressed orally or in a specific statement concerning the quality of the product. It may be a written statement that is given to customers. Jim received a written warranty from the manufacturer and an oral promise from the salesperson. An implied warranty is not written or stated orally. A full warranty is a warranty that covers the entire product; it has no time limit. A limited warranty is a warranty that does not contain the provisions of a full warranty; it may cover certain repairs or specific parts only.

prompt: Procter & Gamble makes laundry detergent, bleach, and fabric softeners, as well as hundreds of other products. The laundry care products constitute a product
explanation: Line. A product line is a group of related product items offered by one manufacturer, such as Procter & Gamble's laundry care products. A product mix is a collection of all the products a manufacturer produces. A product item is a certain model, brand, or size of an individual product in the manufacturer's product line. Product depth is a term that describes the number of different product lines produced by a manufacturer.

prompt: A retailer might bundle products together to sell at a lower price for a limited time in order to
explanation: Encourage future sales. Product bundling involves combining goods and/or services and offering them to customers as one product for a lower price than if the customers were to buy all of the products individually. The reason why retailers bundle products is to get customers to try a product they would not normally purchase. If the customers try the product and like it, they might purchase the product as an unbundled item at another time, which encourages future sales. Retailers do not bundle products so they can limit returns, monitor promotional activities, or eliminate cash shortages.

prompt: When planning the level of stock to have in inventory to satisfy demand, department stores usually adjust for the
explanation: Possibility of error. Department stores plan stock levels in order to have the goods on hand that customers want to buy when they want to buy them. Stores want an appropriate level of inventory to avoid running out, so they often adjust for the possibility of error. For example, if a store expects to sell $300,000 in merchandise one month, it might buy $325,000 worth of merchandise to compensate for possible errors in forecasting sales. Although stores do not want to have too much stock in inventory, they do not want to run out and lose sales because goods are not available for customers to buy. When planning the level of stock to have in inventory to satisfy demand, department stores do not adjust for the value of markdowns, level of desired profit, or time of delivery.

prompt: A retailer decides to reduce the price of an item by 25%. The new price of the item originally marked $65 will be
explanation: $48.75. To calculate the new or discounted price, multiply the original price by the percentage amount to obtain the dollar amount reduction ($65.00 x .25 or 25% = $16.25). Then, subtract the dollar amount reduction from the original price to obtain the new or discounted price ($65 - $16.25 = $48.75).

prompt: Which of the following is not an advantage of a central-buying structure:
choices: A consistent image of merchandise and quality
explanation: Time delays. Time delays are not an advantage of a central-buying structure; rather, they are a disadvantage of this structure. A consistent image of merchandise and quality, discounts through volume purchases, and preferential treatment from suppliers are all advantages of a central-buying structure, in which a central office has the authority and responsibility to make all merchandise purchases for every store in a retail chain.

prompt: What do many retailers develop in order to determine the most appropriate assortment of goods to buy?
explanation: Model stock plan. A model stock plan is a list of items the retailer always keeps in stock. The model stock plan includes the type, style, and quantity of goods that the retailer keeps on hand at all times to meet customer demand. Determining the most appropriate assortment of goods to buy is important because if the retailer doesn't have what customers want, customers might take their business elsewhere. Developing a model stock plan helps a retailer to determine the most appropriate assortment of goods to buy and keep in stock. A requisition is the form used by departments within a business to request the purchase or use of needed goods or services. Evaluating a vendor will not help a retailer to determine what to buy. A price line policy is a guideline for setting prices at predetermined price points.

prompt: Which of the following is an external factor that affects the role of promotion in marketing:
explanation: Government regulations. Government regulations are an external factor affecting promotion by putting restrictions on its use. For example, government regulations prohibit cigarettes from being promoted on television or radio. The product that is to be promoted, the channels of distribution, and the price of the product are all internal factors within the control of the business.

prompt: Which of the following is an overall goal of the promotional mix:
choices: To have the right goods available
explanation: To persuade consumers to buy. Businesses combine or mix the different forms (elements) of promotion in order to create the most effective promotional mix. These elements are advertising, personal selling, publicity, and sales promotion. It is not always possible to convey promotional messages inexpensively. Reducing the business's operating expenses is not an overall goal of the promotional mix. Having the right goods available is a responsibility of product/service management.

prompt: A department store that sponsors a sweepstakes promotion and exaggerates the retail price of the grand prize is engaging in unethical behavior known as
explanation: Value misrepresentation. Value misrepresentation is unethical behavior because the advertiser is not being honest about the cost or value of the prize. For example, a department store provides a television set as a prize for a contest. The store claims that the television is worth $500 but actually retails for $300 at an electronics store. Price discrimination occurs when businesses sell similar products to similar customers at different prices. Benefit exploitation is not a common term used to describe advertising practices; however, the term might be considered similar in meaning to puffery. Puffery is a tactic used by advertisers that exaggerates the positive attributes of a product. Cost fixation is not a term commonly used to describe advertising practices and should not be confused with price fixing.

prompt: One reason for the regulation of promotion is to prevent retailers from
explanation: Making misleading statements. One of the main reasons for the regulation of promotion is to prevent retailers from making misleading statements that may confuse customers. Regulations require retailers to have evidence to support any claims they make about products. For example, a retailer may not advertise that its product will solve certain problems if that is not accurate. There are regulations regarding the use of celebrity endorsements, but the regulations do not prevent retailers from using celebrity endorsements. Regulations do not prevent retailers from advertising discounted prices; however, the information provided must be accurate. The regulation of promotion requires retailers to disclose important facts.

prompt: The most common purchase option for television advertising is
explanation: Participation shows. Because the cost of sponsorship has reached a level that is too costly for many companies, many have chosen to participate as co-sponsors. Spot announcements, a type of local advertising, may appear with a participating announcement but is from a local station. Network affiliation describes the relationship of a station to a sponsor, such as CBS or NBC, but does not involve the use of advertising. Run-of-station, a variation of run-of-paper, is not a form of sponsorship.

prompt: What type of exterior signs do retail stores often create to promote specials that will be in effect for only a short time?
explanation: Banners. Banners are a type of promotional sign that are usually made of fabric, plastic, or paper. They are large and relatively inexpensive as compared to the cost of other types of signs. Therefore, retail stores often use banners to promote specials that will be in effect for only a short time. They can hang the large banners on the exterior of the building to attract attention to the special and then remove them once the special is over. Neon is an expensive and permanent type of sign that would not be used to promote short-term specials. A valance is also a permanent type of sign. Endcaps are interior signs used on the ends of display cases.

prompt: A local department store provides an "angel" tree display during November and early December, from which shoppers can choose the name of an impoverished child for whom shoppers can buy holiday gifts. The shoppers who purchase the children's gifts in the store receive a discount. What use of visual merchandising is being demonstrated?
choices: Introducing the store to prospective customers
explanation: Building goodwill for the business. The use of the "angel" tree builds goodwill for the business by showing its concern for children in the community. Grand-opening activities would introduce the store to prospective customers. A display of merchandise featuring pertinent information such as fabric content and care instructions is another use of visual merchandising. Consumers could be informed of trends through other types of displays.

prompt: An important part of dismantling a display of furniture that is set up on the sales floor is
choices: washing display windows to remove stains.
testing the lighting and replacing bulbs.
vacuuming to pick up pins and staples.
explanation: Vacuuming to pick up pins and staples. Some furniture displays are set up on the sales floor and are changed periodically to promote new merchandise. When dismantling these displays, it is necessary to vacuum the area to pick up pins and staples that may have fallen out during the removal process. For example, fabric may be stapled around tables or throws may be pinned to sofas. The staples and pins often fall out when the pieces are moved. It is necessary to vacuum up these items to prepare the area for another display, or to open it up to customer traffic. A merchandise loan form is prepared before merchandise is used in a display. Testing the lighting and replacing bulbs are functions of display maintenance. A display set up on the sales floor may not be near windows, so washing display windows is unnecessary.

prompt: Which of the following types of merchandise would be effectively displayed in a shadow box:
explanation: Rings or necklaces. Because of their small size and great expense, rings or necklaces can be displayed quite effectively in a shadow box. Often the box is well-lit, and the items will sparkle in the open air or behind glass. Cosmetics are usually displayed in racks so customers can compare the different styles and lines. Clothing is best displayed on mannequins or folded on shelves. Children's toys, although small in nature, are best displayed in an open area where children may handle the items.

prompt: Which of the following usually is included in a business's promotional plan:
explanation: Timetable for completion. A promotional plan is a guide for a business to follow in promoting the company and its goods and services. The plan usually includes a timetable for completion. The timetable specifies when ads will run and when publicity efforts will take place during the life of the promotional plan. The timetable provides structure for the plan. Previous sales figures, a table of organization, and projected profit margins are not included in a business's promotional plan.

prompt: Retail businesses that do not have adequate in-house staff to coordinate large promotional events often must pay for the services of
explanation: Outside agencies. Coordinating large promotional events is an important responsibility that may require the retail business to engage the assistance of outside agencies. Many businesses do not have sufficient in-house staff to handle the everyday promotional activities as well as special events. The responsibility for coordinating large promotional events would not be given to part-time employees or executives even though they are already on the payroll. Retail businesses seldom have volunteers on staff.

prompt: A national retail chain has a toll-free telephone number customers can call if they have product questions. The retail chain's purpose is to
explanation: Help customers determine needs. Retail chains that provide opportunities for two-way communication between customers and salespeople are enabling customers to receive help with their buying decisions. The retail chain wants to help the customer to find the product that best fits his/her needs. Retail chains affect employment levels by increasing or decreasing their hiring. Retail chains can conduct market research or offer credit without a toll-free telephone line.

prompt: One opportunity for salespeople to provide quality customer service after the sales close is to
explanation: Follow up with billing issues. After the sale closes is a critical time for businesses to provide quality customer service. This time of follow-through is often what separates successful businesses from unsuccessful businesses. One way to follow up is to handle any billing or invoicing issues that may arise. Suggesting additional products, promising free repairs, and helping with purchasing decisions are pre-sale opportunities to provide quality customer service.

prompt: Which of the following is not helpful to the retail salesperson in building a clientele:
choices: Having a slight interest in customers
explanation: Having a slight interest in customers. Retail salespeople should have more than a slight interest in customers and their needs. Their interest in the customer and his/her needs should be genuine rather than put on in order to make a sale. Customers are very likely to return to a store whose salespeople seem to care about the customer. Dealing with customer complaints affects future relationships and helps you build a clientele. Keeping in touch and aware of customer needs and wants also leads to customer loyalty. Finally, doing occasional favors for customers sets you apart from other retail salespeople and affects the customer's attitude towards you.

prompt: A customer who returns a unique item that was purchased on credit from a store with a strict return policy is likely to receive a(n)
explanation: Charge credit. A store with a strict return policy may impose time limits for returns or make adjustments for credit only instead of cash. The amount of the purchase will be subtracted from the customer's credit account. There would be no reason for the store to adjust the price since the product is not damaged or defective. An even exchange simply substitutes an item whose value is equal to that of the customer's original purchase. Since this item was unique, it is unlikely that it can be exchanged for another.

prompt: An advantage to a bicycle manufacturer of sales-force automation is that it
choices: prevents sales personnel from making order-entry errors.
provides salespeople with quick access to information.
explanation: Provides salespeople with quick access to information. Sales-force automation refers to the technology that a bicycle manufacturer uses to maximize its sales department's efficiency. For example, a computer can provide salespeople with quick access to a bicycle store's purchasing history or inventory-status information. Sales-force automation does not necessarily prioritize each salesperson's responsibilities, predict long-term sales forecasts accurately, or prevent order-entry errors.

prompt: A salesperson who sells 25 televisions to Store A for one price and 25 televisions to Store B for a higher price is involved in price
explanation: Discrimination. Price discrimination is an illegal activity in which a business charges different customers different prices for similar amounts and types of products. If a salesperson sells the same product in the same amounts to different customers and charges different prices, the salesperson is involved in price discrimination. Price competition is a type of rivalry between or among businesses that focuses on the use of price to attract scarce customer dollars. Charging different prices for the same product is not price segmentation or price misrepresentation.

prompt: When a store's promotional materials are used as sources of selling information, a retail salesperson may need to
explanation: Sort out useful selling facts. A retail salesperson must be able to discriminate between product facts and company "hype" in promotional materials in order to obtain useful, accurate, selling information. Calling the manufacturer's representative, asking other salespeople for help, and using your own personal experience are ways to obtain information that can be used in selling when no promotional materials are available.

prompt: Why do many discount stores sell products that carry a national brand as well as private brand and generic products?
choices: To limit the number of quality items
To maintain a high inventory level
To provide customers with more choices
explanation: To provide customers with more choices. Many discount stores now sell all categories of branded products-manufacturer or national brands, private or store brands, and generic brands. The reason for this is to provide customers with more choices. Some customers always buy the manufacturer's brands, such as Sony and RCA, while others prefer the store's private brand, such as Sears' Kenmore line. Other customers prefer generic products because they usually are the least expensive. If a store sells all the categories of brands, it has a better chance of appealing to a wider market. Customers have more choices and are more likely to find the product they want in the price range they want. The national and private brands are more expensive than generic brands. Stores do not carry all the brand categories in order to maintain a high inventory level or to limit the number of quality items.

prompt: Which of the following is not an example of a nonverbal statement of interest:
explanation: Saying "great!" A nonverbal statement of interest conveys a message through the use of actions rather than words. A smile, a nod, or simply leaning forward are forms of nonverbal statements of interest. Using words is verbal communication.

prompt: The fact that a customer raises a valid objection to a product is evidence of his/her
choices: inability to pay for the item.
explanation: Interest in the product. An objection is a point of difference between a customer and a salesperson that may prevent a sale. It is the customer's reason for not buying, but it also indicates the customer has some degree of interest in the product. Objections are not necessarily reflections of customers' personalities or financial status. The salesperson should not consider a valid objection as a personal attack unless it is delivered in a manner that is obviously intended to be offensive.

prompt: Which closing technique is being used in the following situation: "You'll enjoy using this portable heater this winter to heat your bathroom."
explanation: Suggesting ownership. In the suggesting ownership close, the salesperson stresses the pleasures or benefits of ownership. No customer objection has been stated, and the close is not based on overcoming an objection. Notice how the salesperson's choice of words suggests ownership-"You'll enjoy . . ." In a narrative close, the salesperson tells a story about people who have purchased the good/service. A standing-room-only close infers the product is in short supply or a one-of-a-kind item.

prompt: When selling gift certificates to customers, one reason why it is important for a retailer to spell out the exact dollar value on the certificate is because the certificate is
explanation: The same as cash. A gift certificate is the same as cash because the buyer has paid the retailer a certain amount of money in exchange for the certificate. Consequently, retailers make sure that the exact dollar value of the certificate is spelled out rather than written in numbers. In some cases, the amount may be spelled out and written in numbers to make sure there is no mistake. Gift certificates usually are sold for a specific amount of money although some retailers may occasionally offer a discount if a customer buys a large number of certificates. The money received from the sale of gift certificates is accounted for in the retailer's books, but that is not the reason for spelling out the exact dollar value on the certificate. A debt is money the retailer owes to others.

prompt: When accepting personal checks from customers, what do most retailers require be printed on the checks?
explanation: Name, address, phone number. When accepting personal checks from customers, most retailers will not accept checks that are not printed with the customer's name, address, and phone number. Checks that do not contain this information are often called starter checks and are the first checks a customer receives when opening a checking account. The unprinted checks indicate that the account is new. Most retailers accept only checks that are printed because that indicates that the account has been open for a length of time. Customers handwrite the date and dollar amount and sign the checks. Most personal checks do not contain a person's occupation, title, or Social Security number.
